free_tier.stated: Eligible active accounts can contribute USD 12.50 with a /64 transport prefix or USD 20 with a /80 transport prefix for an additional routed /48.

egress.terms: no traffic allowance is published on the home, request or policy page; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: 'A user chooses a tunnel type, selects the preferred PoP, provides the technical information needed for provisioning'
tooling: OpenVPN, wireguard-tools, or a plain 6in4/GRE/IPIP interface
chaining: the review gate makes it a slow path to the same result a self-service broker gives in a minute; it is worth it only for the /48 or for the BGP option.

limits.value: requests are reviewed by the 6Project team, typically 1-24 hours, before a tunnel is provisioned
prefixes are issued with annual validity and must be renewed before expiry, with only a short grace period
review 1 to 24 hours, up to 72 at peak

binding_note: A person reviews each request before anything is provisioned, so that gate is reached before any byte is transferred and it is what fails first at 1 TiB/month. Renewal is the second gate: a prefix that is not renewed annually is removed after a short grace period.

identity_cost.detail: 'IPv6 tunnel requests must be submitted through the official form. Review time is typically 1-24 hours. Accurate contact details and technical information are required for provisioning.'

reliability_note: 'The tunnel broker operates on a best-effort basis with no guaranteed SLA'; abuse can lead to throttling, suspension or removal.
confidence_note: the transports and the review gate are documented from 6project's own policy page; the prefix a free account actually receives, and its price, are not stated by the vendor and come from two third-party lists that disagree.

evidence.proved: '6Project provides IPv6 tunnels over OpenVPN, WireGuard, 6in4, GRE, and IPIP.'
'IPv6 tunnel requests must be submitted through the official form. Review time is typically 1-24 hours.'
a routed /48 costs USD 12.50 with a /64 transport prefix or USD 20 with a /80
third-party list: '6in4 / GRE Tunnels /64, /80 Prefix', 'Notes: /64 for EUR 11.50/y and /80 for EUR 5.50/y'
third-party list: '1.50 EUR one-time for ::/128, 5.50 EUR one-time for ::/80'
community-operated AS208753 broker; 'Available methods can include OpenVPN, WireGuard, SIT, GRE, IPIP, or BGP depending on the selected location'

notes: The two third-party lists disagree with each other and with the policy page on what is free: tunnelbroker.services says a /64 costs EUR 11.50/year, handwiki says a::/128 costs EUR 1.50 once and a /80 EUR 5.50 once, and the policy page speaks of /64 and /80 accounts as things that already exist when a /48 is bought. A free routed prefix is therefore not established. AS208753, PoPs in Milan, Frankfurt, Vienna, Bradford, Los Angeles, Las Vegas and Wuhan. The routed /48 is USD 12.50 with a /64 transport or USD 20 with a /80, and adds 365 days to the account. The homepage read returned a server-rendered SEO fallback, not the React application; the policies page carried the substance. Re-read 2026-10-23: BGP is available at most locations, and the policies page carries the same sentence as the homepage.

extras.wg_detail: '6Project provides IPv6 tunnels over OpenVPN, WireGuard, 6in4, GRE, and IPIP.' Whether the WireGuard profile is generated or hand-written is not stated.
extras.volume_stated: no traffic allowance is published on the home, request or policy page
extras.transit_note: AS208753 carries the traffic from its own PoPs.
